result:
I’d try to spark a shift in global empathy—encouraging people to genuinely understand and care about one another. When we imagine a world driven by empathy, many deep-rooted challenges begin to shift in perspective. Empathy can inspire us to bridge divides, confront issues like inequality, environmental harm, and conflict with collaboration instead of division.

When people feel truly understood and valued, it transforms how communities, societies, and nations interact. Instead of reacting solely in self-interest or fear, an empathetic approach nudges us toward cooperation and innovative solutions that consider both present needs and future well‑being. This wouldn’t instantly resolve every problem, but it could pave the way toward deeper dialogue, more inclusive decision-making, and a global community that prioritizes collective well‑being alongside individual rights.

In short, if I could change one thing, it would be fostering empathy at all levels—shifting our view from “me” to “we,” so that every person feels responsible for and connected to the world and each other.
